## Generic ghost exchange (`SyncOptions`) {#sec-ch03-exchange}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: src/layout/layout.hpp, src/layout/layout.cpp, src/mesh/meshblock.cpp, tests/test_mesh_exchange.py, tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py

A ghost exchange is the fill of a block's ghost cells from the interior cells of its neighbours; a halo exchange is
the same operation under another name. Every ghost that is not at a physical face (@sec-ch03-physfaces) is filled
by an exchange. A sync packs, for each
direction with a neighbour, the interior slab next to that face into a send buffer, moves the buffers (between
ranks through the communication backend, @sec-ch14-backends, with the message matching and in-process copies of
@sec-ch14-msgmatch), and unpacks each received buffer into the ghost slab of the same direction. By default only face neighbours are
exchanged; afterwards the four $x_2$-$x_3$ ghost corners are filled from the edge strips. The per-stage sync exchanges
the conserved variables of the hydro and, when there are scalars, of the scalar; @sec-ch03-synctype lists the other
syncs. On the cubed sphere the same steps run with interpolation across panel edges (@sec-ch03-csinterp).

`MeshBlockImpl::exchange` orchestrates the block sync through its layout; `LayoutImpl` owns the
packing, remote exchange and finalisation operations, including `LayoutImpl::exchange_remote`
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange >}},
{{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::exchange_remote >}}). See @sec-ch14-msgmatch for the
message matching and in-process copies used by those operations.

Local symbols: $q^{\mathrm{c}}_{k,j}$ a synthesised corner ghost value; $q^{\mathrm{L}}$ and
$q^{\mathrm{B}}$ the ghost strips left ($x_2$ side) and below ($x_3$ side) of a corner, with $j_0$, $k_0$ their
first interior column and row next to the corner; $\iota_a\in\{-1,0,1\}$ the direction of a neighbour along $x_a$, in cells (the code's `offset`).

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** For each neighbour across a face, copy its interior slab of width $n_g$ into this block's ghost slab,
then synthesise each $x_2$-$x_3$ ghost corner as the mean of the two adjacent ghost strips (@eq-ch03-exchange-corner).

**Data.** In: the neighbour's interior cells. Out: ghost slabs and corners, in the units of the synced variables
(conserved by default).

**Placement.** Every block sync: the per-stage conserved sync, the primitive and scalar syncs.

**Activation.** `SyncOptions` (`type`, `skip_corner`, `interpolate`, `dim`, phase flags); default conserved
variables, corners skipped and synthesised, no interpolation.

**Guarantee / limits.** Face copies are exact; the synthesised corner is a convention, exact on a constant and first
order on a gradient.

**Evidence.** `test_exchange`, `test_mesh_exchange_python`, `test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python`;
check `[C15]`; the ctest entries were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

### Derivation

The face exchange is a copy and needs no derivation. The corner is a convention, stated here. With $\iota_a$ the direction of a neighbour along $x_a$, and with the left ghost
strip $q^{\mathrm{L}}$ (offset $\iota_2 = -1$) and the bottom strip $q^{\mathrm{B}}$ (offset $\iota_3 = -1$), the
lower-left corner ghost at $(k, j)$ is

$$
q^{\mathrm{c}}_{k,j} = \tfrac12\left(q^{\mathrm{L}}_{k_0,\,j} + q^{\mathrm{B}}_{k,\,j_0}\right),
$$ {#eq-ch03-exchange-corner}

that is, the mean of the left strip's value in the same $x_2$ column at the row next to the corner and the bottom
strip's value in the same $x_3$ row at the column next to the corner. @eq-ch03-exchange-corner and its three mirror
images are `fill_corners` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::fill_corners >}}). It reproduces a constant field; for a field with a
gradient it is a first-order fill, because both terms are read up to $n_g$ cells away from the corner cell. The
check evaluates @eq-ch03-exchange-corner on every corner ghost of an $n_g = 3$ block: a constant field is
reproduced to exactly zero, and on $q = \alpha + \beta x_2 + \gamma x_3$ the error halves at each refinement
(measured order 1.00, 1.00) and stays under the closed-form bound
$n_g(\Delta x_2|\beta| + \Delta x_3|\gamma|)/2$, with $\Delta x_2 = \Delta x_3$ on the check's grid (`[C15]`).[^exc-c15] The tests below cover the face copies.

[^exc-c15]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    line `[C15]`; a numpy port of `LayoutImpl::fill_corners` at the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

Slabs are addressed by the offset $(\iota_3, \iota_2, \iota_1)$, the direction of the neighbour in cells along
each axis (count); `get_buffer_id` maps an
offset to one of 9 buffers (27 on `cubed`). The sent slab is the $n_g$-wide interior next to the face; the received
slab is the ghost zone across it. With `skip_corner` only offsets with one non-zero component are exchanged. The
`dim` option restricts a sync to one direction (used for face states, @sec-ch03-cslrsync). Physical faces are skipped.
`fill_corners` runs at the end of `finalize` when corners are skipped and the sync is not one phase of a split;
for a split cubed-sphere sync it runs once after both phases. Only $x_2$-$x_3$ corners are synthesised; corners that
involve $x_1$ are not. The per-stage sync runs at the start of `MeshBlock::forward`, before reconstruction reads the
ghosts. @fig-ch03-exchange-stencil shows the slabs and buffer ids.

#| fig-alt: "A block in the centre of a three by three arrangement, numbered 0 to 8, with arrows from the four face neighbours and the corners marked as synthesised."

: Code map of the generic exchange. {#tbl-ch03-exchange-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-exchange-code):

1. `exchange_ghost_zones` syncs `hydro_u` as conserved with interpolation on, then `scalar_s` as scalar
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}).
2. `exchange` takes the two-phase branch on a subdivided cubed sphere
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange >}}), otherwise it calls `_exchange_once`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::_exchange_once >}}). That runs the three phases in turn:
   `begin_exchange` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::begin_exchange >}}), `launch_exchange`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::launch_exchange >}}) and `finalize_exchange`
   ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::finalize_exchange >}}).
3. `serialize` copies each interior slab into the cached send buffer of its `get_buffer_id`
   ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::serialize >}}).
4. `finalize` waits on the messages, calls `deserialize` and then `fill_corners` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::finalize >}}).

**How to use it.** There is no YAML key. The exchange follows from the layout and the boundary names
(@sec-ch03-layouts, @sec-ch03-physfaces), and each caller sets `SyncOptions` in C++. The per-stage sync is
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::exchange_ghost_zones >}}):

```cpp
  SyncOptions sync_opts;
  sync_opts.interpolate(true).type(kConserved);

  Variables sync_vars;
  sync_vars["hydro_u"] = hydro_u;
  exchange(sync_vars, sync_opts);

  if (pscalar->nvar() > 0) {
    sync_opts.type(kScalar);
    sync_vars.clear();
    sync_vars["scalar_s"] = scalar_s;
    exchange(sync_vars, sync_opts);
  }
```

Corners are skipped by default (`skip_corner`) and synthesised by @eq-ch03-exchange-corner in `fill_corners`
({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::fill_corners >}}):

```cpp
  // Fill-in left-bot inter-panel corners
  std::tuple<int, int, int> corner(/*dy=*/-1, /*dx=*/-1, 0);
  auto sub = pmb->part(corner, PartOptions().exterior(true));
  for (auto& [name, var] : vars) {
    auto var_left = var.index(sub_left).select(-3, 0).unsqueeze(-3);
    auto var_bot = var.index(sub_bot).select(-2, 0).unsqueeze(-2);
    var.index_put_(sub, 0.5 * (var_left + var_bot));
  }
```

Nothing is refused: a face without a neighbour keeps its boundary function.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_mesh_exchange_python` | each ghost of a $2\times2$ slab in one process equals its neighbour's payload | exact | integer payloads |
| `test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange_python` | a uniform radial velocity crosses every panel edge unchanged | $10^{-12}$ abs. $+ 10^{-12}$ rel. | round-off of the frame rotations |
| `test_exchange` | ghosts hold the neighbour's payload, two ranks | value bounds | payloads identify the sender |

: Tests of the generic exchange. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-exchange-tests}

The slab check, in the top-level script `test_mesh_exchange.py`, is the final `torch.all` comparison of each ghost
with the rank `neighbor_rank` names ({{< code tests/test_mesh_exchange.py >}}).
The radial-velocity check sets `ABS_TOL` and `REL_TOL` ({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py REL_TOL >}}, {{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py ABS_TOL >}})
and compares the worst ghost error against them with `ideal_match`
({{< code tests/test_cubed_sphere_vertical_velocity_exchange.py main >}}). The two-rank case uses `ghosts_match_expected`
({{< code tests/test_exchange.cpp ghosts_match_expected >}}). The Python tests run on CPU in one process; `test_exchange.release` runs on two
ranks with gloo. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence). No test checks the
synthesised corners.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Corners that involve $x_1$ (blocks split in $x_1$ on `cubed`) are never exchanged or synthesised.
:::

At a physical $x_1$ wall such corners are rewritten by the corner refresh (@sec-ch03-cornerrefresh); at an internal
$x_1$ seam they keep stale values (read from the code; not measured). No dimension-split stencil reads them; a
cross-derivative operator could.
For covariance fluxes feeding interior cells, no stale $x_1$-seam corner is read:
`x1_seam_rows` replaces the one neighboring face-state row across the full transverse extent before the $x_1$ differences,
although vectorized calculations on unused outer ghost rows can still read unrefreshed corners when $n_g > 1$
(`src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp:164–173,705–711,734–746,776–780` and `src/hydro/hydro.cpp:285–317` at `c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f`; {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}, {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_x1_ghost_rows >}}).
The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
